title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Coliseum on 1973-06-22
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v9.12 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of the laid‑back Vancouver ’73 show, highlighted by a stellar Bird Song, the epic He’s Gone > Truckin’ > The Other One sequence and superb Jerry/Keith interplay.
ai_review.review: The June‑22‑1973 PNE Coliseum performance is widely praised for its relaxed, exploratory vibe and top‑tier improvisations – especially the soaring Bird Song, the powerful He’s Gone → Truckin’ → The Other One medley, and a standout Play‑in‑the‑Band.  Charlie Miller’s soundboard mix is crisp and well‑balanced, with only minor quirks (a slightly distracting edit on Bird Song and some Bertha hiss).  Overall both the music and the recording deliver an almost flawless listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 25 reviews (average 4.36★) overwhelmingly praise both performance and sound quality; weighting favors the show, leading to a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with beautiful EQ; Charlie Miller’s work praised. Minor issues noted on Bird Song edit and occasional Bertha hiss, but overall superior sound.

standout_songs: He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: Bird Song (distracting edit for some listeners)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert unfolds slowly at first, then builds into an expansive second set that many describe as unstoppable and tightly paced.  The relaxed West‑Coast vibe gives way to high‑energy jams, delivering a cohesive two‑hour journey.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for gorgeous guitar tone, watery noodling on Black Peter and strong lead throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass solo in the Truckin' jam called “gold”; noted for bombs in Playin', high notes at end of Box, teasing Fire on the Mountain, and overall powerful low‑end presence.
band_member_comments.Bob: Rhythm guitar and vocal work highlighted as solid and supportive, especially during jams and transitions.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano/electric piano lauded for jazzy texture, prominent yet balanced mix; described as a key driver of the show’s energy.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming called tight, crisp and integral to the jazz‑based quintet feel.
